title: Comparatives and Superlatives Quiz 5
description: Every question hides a trap: a double form, a spelling change or a rule exception.
instructions: Comparatives and Superlatives: Difficult: comparatives and superlatives.
Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Which sentence is **NOT** correct?
options: She is the tallest girl here.
She is more taller than me.
She is more careful than me.
She is taller than me.
questions.explanation: Taller is already a comparative. Watch out: more and -er cannot be used together.

questions.question: My bag is {{1}} (heavy) than yours.
questions.explanation: Heavy ends in consonant + y, so y becomes ier. Watch out: not heavyer.

questions.question: 'Quieter' and 'more quiet' are both accepted for the two-syllable adjective 'quiet'.
questions.explanation: A few two-syllable adjectives, such as quiet, clever, simple and narrow, can take both forms. Watch out: this is the exception to the syllable rule.

questions.question: Complete the table.
questions.explanation: Each adjective follows a different spelling rule. Watch out: thin doubles the n, late keeps one t, noisy changes y to i.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: He is the most tallest boy in the class.
accepted: He is the tallest boy in the class.
He is the tallest boy in the class
questions.explanation: Tallest is already a superlative. Watch out: most and -est together are wrong.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: This is easy than I expected.
This is easier than I expected.
This is the easier than I expected.
This is more easier than I expected.
questions.explanation: Easy becomes easier before than. Watch out: easy alone is not a comparative.
Both are true and the reason explains the first: bad does not follow the -er rule. Watch out: badder does not exist.

questions.question: Which is the superlative of 'good'?
options: most good
goodest
best
betterest
questions.explanation: Good is irregular: better, best. Watch out: the superlative also needs the in a sentence: the best student.

questions.question: How many syllables does the word 'dangerous' have?
questions.explanation: dan-ger-ous has three syllables, so it takes more and most. Watch out: count the sounds, not the letters.

questions.question: Which are correct?
options: the most dangerous
the happiest
the more happy
the dangerousest
questions.explanation: Dangerous is long, so the most dangerous; happy changes to the happiest. Watch out: -est never goes on long adjectives.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The more I read, the most I learn.
The more I read, the more I learn.
More I read, more I learn.
The most I read, the most I learn.
questions.explanation: The pattern is the more ..., the more ... with comparatives. Watch out: most is a superlative.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: By far adds emphasis before the superlative. Watch out: the stays before best.
